name: Mica
overview: Mica is a male Levite identified as the son of Zichri, noted specifically in 1 Chronicles 9:15. He is mentioned among those who sealed the covenant document in Nehemiah 10:11, indicating his role in the post-exilic community. His tribal affiliation with Levi highlights his connection to the priestly and temple service lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Mica means 'Who is like y-h-v-h?', reflecting a rhetorical question praising the uniqueness and sovereignty of God. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:15, is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a significant theological meaning within the Hebrew tradition.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Mica as the son of Zichri, with an inferred relationship to Mattaniah as his father or ancestor. These familial ties place him within a known Levite lineage, though no further family details are provided beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Mica's significance lies in his identification as a Levite involved in the covenant renewal during the return from exile, as evidenced by his inclusion on the sealed document in Nehemiah 10:11. His mention in 1 Chronicles 9:15 situates him within the genealogical records that affirm the continuity of the Levitical priesthood. Through these references, Mica represents the faithful remnant committed to God's covenant and temple worship in the post-exilic period.
